plans.name: Pay as you go (serverless, account approval)
plans.note: List GPU prices on fal.ai/pricing, billed per second while runners are alive (SETUP/IDLE/RUNNING/DRAINING). Free account; serverless deploy access is approved per account by fal (docs: "Serverless access is approved per account"). Concurrency quotas not published.

plans.name: Enterprise / custom deployment
plans.note: "As low as" prices (H100 $1.89/h ...) for custom deployments via support@fal.ai.

caveats: GPU time is not interchangeable with model API output pricing. Custom deployment requires contacting support. The as-low-as column is conditional, not generally available on-demand pricing. Serverless CPU/RAM bundles verified in machine-types docs; separate Compute VMs have different shape and unpublished dashboard rates. Billing starts at SETUP and includes IDLE/RUNNING/DRAINING/TERMINATING; PENDING and DOCKER_PULL unbilled. This is not active-request-only pricing.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Serverless GPU regimes are ordinary list-priced GPU instances (alt removed 2026-09-28); reserved regimes stay sales.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Access gate (2026-09-28): fal.ai/docs/documentation/serverless says "Serverless access is approved per account ... the fal team must approve access" (request at fal.ai/dashboard/serverless-get-started). List prices apply once approved; not negotiated, so not flagged sales. Treat as a minor availability caveat.

Further serverless machine types exist with no public price: CPU XS/S/M/L/XL (0.5-8 cores, 0.5-30 GB), GPU-A100 (40 GB, 12 CPU, 60 GB RAM), GPU-L40 (48 GB, 6 CPU, 100 GB RAM); the FAQ also names RTX 4090, RTX 5090, H100 MIG, A100 80GB, L40S. B300 is on the price pages but not in the machine-types doc.
B200 VRAM now 192GB on fal.ai/serverless (fal.ai/pricing still 180GB), resolving the card's 180 vs 192 GB note in favour of the docs.

Two official fal price tables disagree (2026-09-29): fal.ai/pricing (card source) lists B300 $8.50, B200 $6.25, H200 $4.50, H100 $4.50, RTX PRO 6000 $2.99, while fal.ai/serverless lists B300 $12.99, GB200 $9.99, B200 $7.99, H200 $6.00, H100 $4.50, RTX PRO 6000 $4.00. Card GPU rates may be 28-53% low except H100; fal says to contact sales for the latest pricing.

Serverless billing tail: keep_alive defaults to 60 s of billed IDLE time per runner spin-up (configurable, 0 allowed); termination_grace_period defaults to 5 s (max 1 h) and is billed; min_concurrency runners bill 24/7; 5xx responses are not charged; multi-GPU is billed gpu_count x duration. Short sporadic requests therefore pay about 60+ s of GPU each unless keep_alive is lowered.

fleet.verification: fal team approves Serverless access per account; request through serverless-get-started dashboard.
fleet.notes: Confirmed: Model API account concurrency (new accounts 2 concurrent requests, self-serve up to 40 as credit purchases grow, above 40 via sales) does NOT apply to your own Serverless endpoints; their runner count is capped by your own max_concurrency. Serverless deploy access still needs per-account approval. No published GPU quota for Serverless.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When a new runner starts and calls setup(), it can load model weights from /data instead of downloading them from scratch.
snapshot_auto.note: Serverless runners are stateless containers: every new runner re-runs setup() (cold start); only files written to the shared /data FS persist. No checkpoint/restore of runner state or memory is documented. Compute instances (dedicated H100) have no stop/snapshot lifecycle in the API (create/list/get/delete only).

harness_api.quote: Use `createFalClient(...).agent` to submit tasks, handle user input, and retrieve generated media.
harness_api.note: The fal Agent SDK (alpha) drives fal's own hosted creative/media agent (conversations, streamed response snapshots, plans, approvals), which uses a private per-user Python sandbox as a tool. It is not an API to run Claude Code/Codex/etc. inside your own serverless runner or Compute instance, so it does not count for the card's GPU product.

ingress_rules.quote: **Private** is the default for `fal deploy`. Only the account owner and their team members can call the app, and they must include an API key.
ingress_rules.note: Serverless apps are reached only via the fal.run gateway; app_auth = private (API key, default for deploy) / public (no auth, default for fal run) / shared (callers pay with own key). A custom server's single exposed_port is routed through the same gateway. No IP allowlists. Compute instances get a public IP with SSH-key login; no documented cloud firewall.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are injected into your runners as environment variables when they start. You access them via `os.getenv()` just like any other environment variable.
secret_proxy.note: Plain env-var secret store, per-environment scoping and a per-app `secrets` allowlist; FAL_KEY auto-injected for privileged apps. No outbound credential-injecting proxy. (fal Agent 'Connectors' run through a hosted integration layer so the agent never sees app passwords, but that is fal Agent's OAuth tooling, not a sandbox egress proxy.)

volume_attach.quote: Every fal runner has access to a persistent `/data` volume. This is a distributed filesystem that is shared across all your apps and runners, linked to your fal account.
volume_attach.note: One account-wide network FS (local NVMe + datacenter cache + global object store), auto-mounted; `data_mounts` can restrict an app to subpaths (e.g. ["/data/.cache"]). No separately sized/attachable block volumes; Compute instances only have their local 1 TB/8 TB SSD.

volume_shared.quote: Since `/data` is shared across all runners, you should be careful when multiple runners write to the same path simultaneously.
volume_shared.note: read-write from all runners of all apps in the account concurrently; also reachable via fal files CLI / Platform API / dashboard.

isolation.quote: Both approaches produce the same kind of runner, and support all the same scaling, observability, and deployment features.
isolation.note: Serverless (the card's primary product) runs your app in a container-based 'runner' per fal's own runner/lifecycle docs. fal Compute (dedicated instances, a secondary mode) is a separate full-VM product reached via SSH; the card models fal primarily as the serverless GPU container product.

image_oci.quote: When you need full control over the environment, use a Dockerfile... You can also pull from private registries (Docker Hub, Google Artifact Registry, AWS ECR, Azure Container Registry) with authentication.
image_oci.note: Custom container images built from a Dockerfile or pulled from external/private OCI registries are a first-class deploy path.

docker_inside.quote: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y ... Install your required software stack
docker_inside.note: fal Compute instances are plain Ubuntu VMs with full sudo/root SSH access, so Docker can be installed and run inside; not explicitly documented as pre-supported, and Serverless runners (already containers) do not document running nested Docker.

desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU inference/training compute, not a graphical desktop product)

egress_ip_type.note: Derived: fal runs on GCP cloud infrastructure and documents no residential/mobile egress IP product; ordinary datacenter egress IPs are assumed.

ssh.quote: Connect via SSH (replace with your actual connection details) ssh ubuntu@your-instance-ip
ssh.note: SSH access is documented for fal Compute instances. Serverless runners are not SSH-accessible.

snapshot.quote: When a new runner starts and calls setup(), it can load model weights from /data instead of downloading them from scratch.
snapshot.note: Serverless runners are stateless containers with no documented checkpoint/restore of runner memory/process state; Compute instance API is documented as create/list/get/delete only, with no snapshot mechanism.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Instances are billed per-hour at fixed rates, so your costs are predictable regardless of how you use the GPU.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI snapshot or checkpoint action is documented for either Serverless runners or Compute instances.

fork.quote: Provisioning an instance takes about 2-3 minutes. You choose an instance type... and click create.
fork.note: No clone/fork-a-machine capability is documented; each Compute instance or Serverless runner is created fresh.

fork_running.quote: Provisioning an instance takes about 2-3 minutes.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: When a new runner starts and calls setup(), it can load model weights from /data instead of downloading them from scratch.

pause_resume.quote: Compute instances run continuously regardless of utilization.
pause_resume.note: Compute instances have no documented stop/pause-with-reduced-billing action (card notes the API is create/list/get/delete only); Serverless's scale-to-zero is a separate automatic-idle feature, not a user pause/resume action.

wake_on_request.quote: Runners spin up when requests arrive and shut down when idle.
wake_on_request.note: Serverless runners scale from zero automatically on incoming requests (cold start).

persistent_disk.quote: Every fal runner has access to a persistent /data volume... linked to your fal account.
persistent_disk.note: Files on /data persist across runner restarts and deploys; Compute instances also keep their attached SSD while running.

live_resize.quote: machine_type: GPU/CPU instance type for your runners.
live_resize.note: machine_type (CPU/RAM/GPU shape) is a static app-level setting; no documented way to resize a running runner or Compute instance in place.

agent_harnesses.quote: Use createFalClient(...).agent to submit tasks, handle user input, and retrieve generated media.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. fal ships an SDK for its own hosted creative/media agent, not preinstalled coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) in the sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Use createFalClient(...).agent to submit tasks, handle user input, and retrieve generated media.
own_agent_api.note: The fal Agent SDK drives fal's own hosted creative/media agent (task submission, streamed responses, generated media) which runs on a private per-user sandbox as a tool.

lang_python.quote: Install the fal CLI with pip install fal and authenticate.
lang_python.note: fal's core Serverless product is a Python framework/runtime (fal.App); Python is the primary supported language.

lang_node.note: First-party Node.js/JS client SDK (@fal-ai/client) is published for calling fal from Node; custom containers can also run a Node.js server directly (docs list Node.js as a supported non-Python runtime via Custom Container).

public_ipv4.quote: ssh ubuntu@your-instance-ip ... Example connection ssh ubuntu@203.0.113.10
public_ipv4.note: Compute instances are reachable at a per-instance IP for SSH; Serverless apps are reached only through the fal.run gateway (no per-runner public IPv4).

egress_http_rules.quote: Private is the default for fal deploy. Only the account owner and their team members can call the app.
egress_http_rules.note: fal documents inbound access-control modes (private/public/shared app_auth) but no outbound HTTP method/path-level egress rules.

guest_firewall.quote: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
guest_firewall.note: derived: Compute instances are full Ubuntu VMs with sudo/root SSH access, so nftables/iptables would work inside; not separately documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Runners spin up when requests arrive and shut down when idle.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented; Serverless runners are ephemeral containers spun up per traffic.

windows.quote: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All documented machine types (Serverless and Compute) are Linux/Ubuntu-based; no Windows option exists.

macos.quote: GPU Machine Types ... GPU-A100, GPU-L40, GPU-H100, GPU-RTXPRO6000, GPU-H200, GPU-B200
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only Linux NVIDIA GPU/CPU machine types are offered; no macOS machines.

arm64.quote: GPU Machine Types ... CPU Machine Types ... XS, S, M, L, XL
arm64.note: All published CPU/GPU machine types pair with NVIDIA GPU hosts; no ARM64 instance type is listed.

self_host.quote: fal Compute gives you dedicated GPU instances... fal Serverless deploys your own Python apps and models on fal GPUs.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. fal is a hosted SaaS platform; no self-hosted/on-prem deployment of the platform itself is offered.

byoc.quote: Private model hosting: Host your proprietary models securely on our infrastructure.
byoc.note: Enterprise 'private model hosting' runs on fal's own infrastructure, not deployed into the customer's cloud account; no BYOC offering is documented.

open_source.quote: fal Compute gives you dedicated GPU instances... fal Serverless deploys your own Python apps and models on fal GPUs.
open_source.note: The core fal platform (Serverless/Compute) is a proprietary hosted SaaS; not offered as an OSI-licensed self-hostable product.

soc2.quote: Fal's Latest SOC 2 Type II Report is Available ... Compliance SOC 2 Type II
soc2.note: fal maintains a Trust Center listing an active SOC 2 Type II report.

sso.quote: Single Sign-On (SSO): Securely integrate with your identity provider and enable users to log in with SSO.
sso.note: SSO is a listed Enterprise plan feature.

max_session_h.quote: Compute instances stay running for as long as you need them.
max_session_h.note: Compute instances run indefinitely until manually stopped; Serverless runners similarly have no documented maximum lifetime cap (only idle/keep_alive/grace-period timers, not a session cap).

nested_virt.quote: PENDING -> Runner is waiting to be scheduled on available hardware; DOCKER_PULL -> Pulling Docker images from registry (if using custom container)
nested_virt.note: not offered: fal Serverless runs your code as a Docker container (custom or managed runtime) scheduled onto shared GPU hosts (isolation=container per card); no docs mention /dev/kvm, nested virtualization, or running VMs/emulators inside a runner. Dedicated Compute VMs are also undocumented on this point. Outside what a container-based serverless GPU product exposes.

egress_allowlist.quote: **Private** is the default for `fal deploy`. Only the account owner and their team members can call the app, and they must include an API key.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: fal's documented network controls (app_auth private/public/shared, per-app secrets scoping) all govern INBOUND access to the deployed endpoint via the fal.run gateway. No docs (deployment, environment-variables, container-setup, or the docs index) describe outbound/egress allowlists, deny-lists, no-internet mode, or security-group egress rules for runners or Compute instances.

hipaa.note: not offered: fal's Trust Center (Vanta-backed) lists only SOC 2 Type II under Compliance, and the fal.ai/enterprise security section names SOC2 Certification, SSO, and general data-privacy commitments but never mentions HIPAA or a BAA. No HIPAA-eligibility statement found anywhere in fal's docs, security, or enterprise pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: `FAL_REGION` | The region where the runner is executing (e.g., `us-east`)
eu_data_residency.note: not offered: the card's own `regions` field is empty and no fal page (machine-types, deploy-to-production, environment-variables, trust center, enterprise) documents a customer-selectable region or an EU-specific region/data-residency guarantee; the only documented region example is us-east with runner placement decided by fal's scheduler.

usage_api.quote: Billing starts at SETUP and includes IDLE/RUNNING/DRAINING/TERMINATING; no API documented for retrieving per-sandbox usage data. Dashboard shows usage but no programmatic access to billable metrics per sandbox or by label.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; fal bills per-second but offers no documented REST API, SDK method, or CLI command to retrieve billable usage for individual sandboxes/runners. The dashboard and pricing model exist but are account-level only.
